column1: # HumanityOS Container Materials (what a container's contact surface is made of)
# section 6 table and the sources it cites). One row per material; a container
# type's `base_material` in types.csv names one of these ids.
#   food_grade    - true if food and drinking water may touch it at all.
#   absorbent     - true if it soaks up what it holds (plastics
#   memory_fills  - how many fills a CLEANED absorbent container still carries
#                   a trace of its previous content into. Codex (bulk edible-oil
#                   tanks. Wood's 3 is an inference (liquid soaks ~8 mm into
#                   staves; no cleaning route is published)
#   refuses       - pipe-separated content traits this material must not store:
#                   water without a liner). Empty = no trait restriction.

column7: Milk, water, beer and most foods; strong brines and salty foods belong in 316
As 304, plus brines, cheese brine and salty foods
Inert: water, acidic foods, fermenting; breaks
Crocks for fermenting and storage while the glaze is lead-free and intact
Water, dry foods, brining; absorbs what it held, so fuel, oil, solvent or cleaner means never food again
Drinks and water bottles; absorbs like HDPE; weakens with repeated reuse
Tubs and food bins; absorbs like HDPE
Dry foods and short contact; not for storing acidic or salty food
Non-acidic foods only; never below about pH 6, never edible oils or milk
Dry goods and grain; never acidic foods; drinking water only with a liner
Fuel and oil drums, tools, gas cylinders; rusts wet; not a food store
Foods within the lining's range; the organic lining remembers previous loads longer than stainless (Codex: 2 loads)
Traditional wine, beer and whole produce; soaks liquid about 8 mm deep (memory 3 is an inference)
Whole produce and dry goods in crates; soaks up spills
Sacks of grain and dry goods; soaks up spills
